answers.children: Tibetan Spaniels are moderately good with children when raised together. Their small 9-15 lb build and independent nature mean they can become overwhelmed by rough play or sudden movements, and their history as watchful monastery sentinels leaves them less tolerant of chaotic energy. Families therefore need calm, respectful youngsters who allow the dog its space on high perches. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Tibetan Spaniels usually get along with other pets if introduced carefully. Their alert and loyal temperament supports peaceful coexistence within the family pack, though their aloofness with strangers can extend to new animals and create initial tension. Owners often see them accept familiar household cats or dogs while remaining watchful.
answers.exercise: Tibetan Spaniels need 20 to 30 minutes of daily exercise. Two short walks plus indoor play keep their moderate energy satisfied, as their short legs and ancient companion role make them unsuited to long hikes or rough terrain. Without it they display sudden indoor zoomies and become restless.
answers.shedding: Yes — Tibetan Spaniels shed moderately year-round. Their medium silky coat with its lion-like mane around the neck traps loose hair on furniture and clothing, and the silky texture requires regular removal of undercoat to prevent mats. This means daily quick brushing becomes part of life with the breed.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Tibetan Spaniel has a medium silky coat that sheds moderately and spreads fine hairs around the house. Its lion-like mane around the neck requires regular grooming to prevent mats, especially behind the ears and on the feathering of the legs. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic and the Tibetan Spaniel is not among those usually suggested to allergy sufferers. (PawLabs shedding score: 5/10)
answers.training: Tibetan Spaniels are moderately easy to train. They grasp what is being asked quickly enough, then decide whether to bother — a legacy of centuries spent as monastery watchdogs making their own judgements from a windowsill. Short sessions with something in it for them work; drilling does not, and they will simply walk away.
answers.lifespan: Tibetan Spaniels live 12-15 years. Their small build and moderate health robustness support a typical small-breed span, though their ancient Tibetan origins and watchful nature give no special immunity to the effects of weight gain or reduced activity in later life.
answers.size: Adult Tibetan Spaniels weigh 9-15 lb and stand 9-11 in tall. Their compact, sturdy proportions let them leap onto counters and the backs of sofas with surprising agility, creating a dog that feels both portable and ever-present as it surveys the household from its chosen high vantage points.
answers.barking: Tibetan Spaniels bark frequently. Bred as sentinels in Tibetan monasteries, they alert to any unusual sound or visitor with sharp, persistent barking that reflects their deeply loyal yet aloof temperament toward strangers. This watchdog instinct remains strong even in modern homes.
answers.apartment: Yes — Tibetan Spaniels adapt well to apartment living. Their moderate energy is satisfied by short daily walks, their small size makes them easy to manage indoors, and their independent nature allows them to settle on perches without needing constant attention, though barking at noises can disturb neighbours.
answers.first-time: Tibetan Spaniels are not the easiest choice for first-time owners. Their independent temperament, tendency toward separation anxiety, and stubbornness during training demand consistent patience and experience that novices may lack, while the strong watchdog instincts can produce more barking than a beginner expects.
